title: Push notifications on phones and their real limits
when: The user wants the phone app to receive push messages and needs the client code, the permission flow and a frank list of what push cannot promise.
prompt:
Goal: A working push path (subscribe, store, send, show, open) with a permission ask at the right moment and the platform limits written down.
Steps:
1. Channel: web push via the service worker, or @capacitor/push-notifications in the store app; both need your server to send.
2. Ask only after a tap on "Notify me about replies"; Notification.requestPermission() resolves "granted", "denied" or "default".
3. Web: reg.pushManager.subscribe({ userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey }) with the VAPID public key; POST the subscription JSON to the server.
4. The server signs with the VAPID private key from an env variable and drops subscriptions answering 404 or 410.
5. sw.js: on "push" event.waitUntil(self.registration.showNotification(title, { body, tag, data: { url } })); on "notificationclick" call clients.openWindow(data.url).
6. Native: PushNotifications.requestPermissions(), register(), then the "registration" event gives the device token.
7. Limits: on one phone OS web push needs the app on the home screen; delivery can be late or dropped; users revoke anytime; native push needs vendor credentials and a developer account.
Quality bar:
- Every push carries a url that opens the right screen.
Pitfalls:
- Asking for permission on first load, which gets a permanent "denied".
Verify:
- [ ] Permission is requested inside a click handler.
- [ ] sw.js handles push and notificationclick.
- [ ] No private key in any client file.
Output: push.js, the push handlers in sw.js and a LIMITS section in the README.

examples.input: quero mandar notificação push pro celular quando chegar mensagem
examples.output: Subscribe after tap, VAPID key from env, sw.js push and click handlers, README limits section
